newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-UNITED OUTPLAYED BY LIVERPOOL BUT STILL WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-UNITED OUTPLAYED BY LIVERPOOL BUT STILL WIN.

text.p: Manchester United became the first team to beat Liverpool this season thanks to a 23rd minute goal from David Beckham which gave the champions a 1-0 English premier league win on Saturday morning.
But Liverpool left Old Trafford wondering how they had lost after dominating almost the entire match, outpassing United in midfield and squandering at least six good scoring chances.
United's goal came from their only serious chance and reflected something of the charmed life United lived throughout a pulsating Lancashire derby played out in front of a capacity 55,000 crowd.
Beckham, standing on the edge of the penalty area, rifled the ball past Liverpool goalkeeper David James but his effort went in off James's right-hand post.

The match, which kicked off at the unusual time of 1015 GMT for a live satellite TV transmission, featured 15 players who had been on World Cup duty in midweek. But none of them looked unduly fatigued by their excursions and the play was full of the passion and drama typical of the biggest fixture in the English domestic programme.

Liverpool's Steve McManaman had three clear-cut scoring chances, their Czech striker Patrick Berger two and striker Stan Collymore one. But in the end they could not turn their territorial superiority into goals as United chalked up their 36th home league match without defeat to become the only unbeaten side in the premier league this season.

Manchester United: 1-Peter Schmeichel; 2-Gary Neville, 19- Ronny Johnsen, 4-David May, 3-Denis Irwin; 10-David Beckham, 7- Eric Cantona, 8-Nicky Butt, 15-Karel Poborsky (18-Paul Scholes 55), 20-Ole Gunnar Solskjaer (11-Ryan Giggs 81), 14-Jordi Cruyff.

Liverpool: 1-David James; 23-John Scales (11-Jamie Redknapp 81), 20-Stig Inge Bjornebye, 4-Jason McAteer, 21-Dominic Matteo, 6-Phil Babb; 7-Steve McManaman, 8-Stan Collymore, 16-Michael Thomas; 10-John Barnes, 15-Patrik Berger.
